title: Compatible systems describe sheaves on the coherent total site
statement: Let $I$ be a small category, let $(\mathcal C_i,u_\alpha)$ be the coherent contravariant pseudofunctor of sites and let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{tot}}$ be the generated-topology total site of [lem-trf-slice-site-total-pseudofunctor]. Assume moreover that every $u_\alpha$ defines a morphism of sites, that is, its left adjoint on sheaves of sets preserves finite limits. For each $\alpha:i\to j$, write $f_\alpha:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_j)$ for the geometric morphism induced by $u_\alpha$. Then $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{tot}})$ is equivalent to the category of systems $(F_i,t_\alpha)$ consisting of a sheaf $F_i$ on each $\mathcal C_i$ and transition maps $t_\alpha:f_\alpha^{-1}F_j\to F_i$ satisfying $t_{\mathrm{id}}$ and the composition cocycle after inserting the unitors and compositors. Under this equivalence, restriction to a fibre is $F\mapsto F_i$, and a morphism of systems is a family of component maps commuting with every $t_\alpha$. The unitors and compositors of the inverse-image functors are the canonical adjunction-compatible comparisons induced by those of the $u_\alpha$. The transition maps $t_\alpha$ are not required to be isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09WF, lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site (the compatible-family description); coherence follows from Tag 09WC Case A

proof.text: Write $e_i:u_{\mathrm{id}_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ and $c_{\alpha,\beta}:u_\alpha u_\beta\xrightarrow{\sim}u_{\beta\alpha}$ for the supplied coherence maps. Put $R_\alpha F=F\circ u_\alpha$ and $L_\alpha=(u_\alpha)_s$. Continuity gives a sheaf $R_\alpha F$, and the sheaf adjunction gives $L_\alpha\dashv R_\alpha$. The compositor induces $d_{\alpha,\beta}:R_{\beta\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_\beta R_\alpha$, whose value at $F,V$ is $F(c_{\alpha,\beta,V})$; the unit gives $r_i:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{\mathrm{id}_i}$, with value $F(e_{i,V})$. These satisfy coherence because $e,c$ do and $F$ is contravariant. The conjugate-isomorphism lemma applied to the composite adjunction gives the unit-compatible comparison $a_{\alpha,\beta}:L_\alpha L_\beta\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\beta\alpha}$; comparing $L_{\mathrm{id}}\dashv R_{\mathrm{id}}$ with the identity adjunction gives $l_i:L_{\mathrm{id}_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$. The adjoint-composition coherence lemma supplies the associativity of $a$ from that of $d$; the two unit laws follow by the same uniqueness applied to a composite with the identity adjunction. Thus these are the specified inverse-image comparisons, without strictifying the diagram.

source.place: Tag 09WF, lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site and its preceding discussion, Case A; with Tag 09WC, lemma-simplicial-site-site.

proof.text:
Transpose $t_\alpha:L_\alpha F_j\to F_i$ under the sheaf adjunction to $s_\alpha:F_j\to R_\alpha F_i$. With $\gamma=\beta\alpha$, the transition cocycle $t_\gamma a_{\alpha,\beta}=t_\alpha L_\alpha(t_\beta)$ is equivalent to
$$d_{\alpha,\beta,F_i}s_\gamma=R_\beta(s_\alpha)s_\beta.$$
Indeed the composite-adjunction Hom bijection sends the right side of the first equality to $R_\beta(s_\alpha)s_\beta$, using naturality of the first Hom bijection in $F_j$; the unit equation defining $a$ sends its left side to $d_{\alpha,\beta,F_i}s_\gamma$. Both Hom bijections are injective, so this proves the equivalence in both directions. Similarly $t_{\mathrm{id}_i}=l_{i,F_i}$ corresponds to $s_{\mathrm{id}_i}=r_{i,F_i}$. Naturality of the Hom bijection also says that a family $h_i:F_i\to G_i$ commutes with the $t$ maps exactly when $R_\alpha(h_i)s^F_\alpha=s^G_\alpha h_j$. Hence it suffices to construct the equivalence with systems in the $s$ form.

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$ on the total site define $F_i(U)=F(i,U)$, restricting along the vertical embedding. A vertical arrow associated to $v:U\to V$ is represented by $(\mathrm{id}_i,e_{i,V}^{-1}v)$. Its composition law is the ordinary fibre composition by the unitor laws. A matching family on a fibre covering extends to its generated total sieve: at an arrow factoring through one covering member, restrict that member's section; independence follows by the total pullback of two covering members, which is their fibre pullback by the total-site lemma. The total sheaf condition gives a unique amalgamation, so $F_i$ is a sheaf. Covering sieves generated by vertical families are covering by the definition of the generated topology; the general precoverage criterion also applies with the identity pullback. This uses only covering pullbacks, not arbitrary fibre products in $I$ or in the total category.

source.place: Tag 09WF, lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site and its preceding discussion, Case A; with Tag 09WC, lemma-simplicial-site-site.

proof.text:
For $V\in\mathcal C_j$ let $k_{\alpha,V}:(i,u_\alpha V)\to(j,V)$ be the arrow $(\alpha,\mathrm{id})$. Set $s_{\alpha,V}=F(k_{\alpha,V})$. For $v:V\to W$ the equality of total arrows $k_{\alpha,W}\circ\iota_i(u_\alpha v)=\iota_j(v)\circ k_{\alpha,V}$ proves naturality, so $s_\alpha:F_j\to R_\alpha F_i$. The composition formula in the total category gives
$$k_{\beta,W}k_{\alpha,u_\beta W}=k_{\beta\alpha,W}\,\iota_i(c_{\alpha,\beta,W}).$$
Contravariance of $F$ therefore yields $R_\beta(s_\alpha)s_\beta=d_{\alpha,\beta,F_i}s_{\beta\alpha}$. Also $k_{\mathrm{id}_i,V}=\iota_i(e_{i,V})$, so $s_{\mathrm{id}_i,V}=F_i(e_{i,V})$. This is precisely the identity and composition law in step 2. All vertical embeddings here include the unitor; none is treated as a strict identity.

source.place: Tag 09WF, lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site and its preceding discussion, Case A; with Tag 09WC, lemma-simplicial-site-site.

proof.text:
Conversely take a system in $s$ form and define a presheaf by $P(i,U)=F_i(U)$ and
$$P(\alpha,f)=F_i(f)\,s_{\alpha,V}:F_j(V)\to F_i(U)\quad(f:U\to u_\alpha V).$$
For $(\alpha,f):(i,U)\to(j,V)$ and $(\beta,g):(j,V)\to(k,W)$, naturality and the $s$ cocycle give
$$F_i(f)s_{\alpha,V}F_j(g)s_{\beta,W}=F_i(f)F_i(u_\alpha g)s_{\alpha,u_\beta W}s_{\beta,W}=F_i(c_{\alpha,\beta,W}u_\alpha(g)f)s_{\beta\alpha,W}.$$
The last expression is $P$ of the composite arrow by the total-site formula. The identity arrow is $(\mathrm{id}_i,e_{i,U}^{-1})$, and its image is $F_i(e_{i,U}^{-1})F_i(e_{i,U})=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $P$ is a presheaf. For a vertical arrow $\iota_i(v)$ the same cancellation gives $P(\iota_i(v))=F_i(v)$, so its fibre restriction is exactly $F_i$.

proof.text: Let $J$ be the precoverage whose presieves are the sets of arrows of vertical covering families. To apply the generated-precoverage criterion, fix such a family $\{V_b\to V\}$ in $\mathcal C_j$ and $q=(\alpha,f):(i,U)\to(j,V)$. Its pulled-back generated sieve $S=q^*\langle V_b\to V\rangle$ is generated by the vertical covering family $B_b=U\times_{u_\alpha V}u_\alpha V_b\to U$ of the total-site lemma: an arrow belongs to $S$ exactly when it factors through one of these projections, by the pullback universal property. Given a matching family $x$ on $S$, its values on these projections agree on their fibre pairwise pullbacks. Glue them uniquely in the sheaf $F_i$ to $z\in F_i(U)=P(i,U)$. For any arrow $a:(h,T)\to(i,U)$ in $S$, pull the $B_b$ covering back along $a$. This is a vertical covering of $T$ in $\mathcal C_h$. On each of its members the equality $P(a)z=x_a$ follows from the matching-family identity and the already known values on $B_b$. Separatedness of $F_h$ gives the equality on $T$. Uniqueness follows from the covering $B_b\to U$. Thus every such pullback sieve has a unique amalgamation, and the cited criterion proves that $P$ is a sheaf for the generated total topology. Empty covering families are included: their unique matching family glues because the corresponding fibre sheaf has one section on that object.

source.place: Tag 09WF, lemma-describe-sheaves-simplicial-site-site and its preceding discussion, Case A; with Tag 09WC, lemma-simplicial-site-site.

proof.text:
A component family $h_i:F_i\to G_i$ satisfying the $s$-compatibility defines $h_{(i,U)}=h_i(U)$. Naturality for $(\alpha,f)$ follows from
$$h_i(U)F_i(f)s^F_{\alpha,V}=G_i(f)h_i(u_\alpha V)s^F_{\alpha,V}=G_i(f)s^G_{\alpha,V}h_j(V).$$
Conversely any natural transformation of total sheaves restricts to $h_i$, and naturality at $k_{\alpha,V}$ gives this compatibility. Thus these operations are inverse on morphisms and preserve identities and composition. On objects, reconstructing from a total sheaf recovers all values and all restriction maps, since every $(\alpha,f)$ factors as $k_{\alpha,V}\circ\iota_i(f)$. Restricting a reconstructed sheaf recovers $F_i$ by step 5 and $s_\alpha$ by evaluation at $(\alpha,\mathrm{id})$. The adjunction bijections in step 2 recover the original $t_\alpha$. These identifications are natural by the same component formula, so the two functors are quasi-inverse and give the claimed equivalence, with the stated fibre restriction and morphisms.
